newsitem.title: ZAIRE: War spreads to Zaire's Shaba province -officials.
newsitem.headline: War spreads to Zaire's Shaba province -officials.

text.p: Rebel fighting has spread to Zaire's mineral-producing Shaba province with the army battling to hold on to the lake-side town of Kalemie, a senior defence ministry official said in Kinshasa on Monday.

"Since last night there has been heavy fighting in the northern part of Kalemie," the official told Reuters. "The FAZ (Zaire army) controls it but reinforcements are having to be sent in from the military base at Kamina."

Military sources in the region said rebels had already seized Kalemie, birthplace of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, on Sunday after heavy fighting between government troops and Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).

Last week the Zairean military said a column of rebels backed up by regular troops from the Rwandan and Burundian armies, had reached Lulimba, around 120 km (70 miles) from Kalemie and near the Shaba border.
The official added that rebels had taken the town of Watsa in Upper Zaire north of Kalemie but that foreign mercenaries backing the army were defending the airport there.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting along with ethnic Tutsis who launched an armed rebellion last October and have since seized several towns in eastern Zaire.
